summary: The contract holds together. instruction.md names manual HC-4 as the authority, and HC-4 plus the README define every graded key, band, rounding rule, order and tolerance. The two gaps the manual leaves (a survey below three quarters of its shift, and the counted level of a reading above 115 dBA) are settled by the instruction's keep-today's-step rule, worked from the manual's own sampled time and measured dose. I traced every sealed expectation and differential pair I read against that combined contract and found no hidden convention, contradiction or test/instruction mismatch.
checks_performed: For each graded key (survey, id, group, dose, twa, status, ceiling, impulse, and the order of both lists), found the defining sentence in instruction.md, the manual (sections 1-6) or the README Report section
Mapped each of the 22 tests to its manual rule, or to the instruction's keep-today's-step clause for the three tests on figures the manual leaves open

Checked the keep-today's-step clause (instruction.md:3) against shift.py and runs.py. Below three quarters: today's step scales to 480 minutes when sampled time is under 480, returns nought when it is 0 and otherwise keeps the measured dose, worked from the manual's sampled time (2.4) and measured dose (3.2). Above the ceiling: the reading is counted at min(level, 115.0)

Traced sealed expectations by hand: below_three_quarters X1, X2, Y2, Y5 and V1 (V1 shows sampled time includes readings from 40 to 79.9 dBA, 240 not 120), V2 with a 0.0 run; above_ceiling Y1, Z1 and K1 counted at 115; sampled_time B1 and B2; threshold A1; twa A4 (1,440 minutes at 97 dBA gives 4800 and 101.8); status S2, S3, T0-T3; rounding R0-R4

Checked all 11 differential pairs: each pair differs only in shift_minutes (below three quarters, both sides stay below three quarters) or in a level above 115 against exactly 115.0 (above ceiling, both sides a whole-shift survey). Neither differing field is used by the kept step, so a contract-following candidate gets equal doses on both sides

Checked TWA rounding margins in the sealed data I traced; none lies near an exact .x5 boundary (smallest margin seen is about 0.005, for L280 at 84.955), so the half-up rule and different float formulas cannot split the expected tenth there
Checked group order: plain ASCII ordering of codes ('0' < '9A' < 'A' < 'A1B2C3D4' < 'AB' < 'ZZ') matches the README's 'ascending character order, digits before letters'
Checked that group rows must not carry ceiling or impulse keys (the verifier rejects them) against manual 6.1 ('a group carries no ceiling or impulse flag')
Checked the dose tolerance: the verifier's 5e-11 lies inside the instruction's band (pass within 1e-11, fail beyond 1e-10); twa is compared exactly, which the instruction discloses
Checked the byte-identical driver requirement (instruction.md:1) against test_submitted_driver_unchanged and the test.sh cmp
Checked that the relabelling (new ids and names, shuffled workers, runs split at the same level) changes no figure the manual defines, and that the generated family declares no trap inputs
Checked that the within_limits and trap_inputs gates keep every graded survey inside manual 1.4 and inside the input kinds its family declares

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule has a candidate-visible authority
coverage_sweep.reason: The 85 dBA criterion with a 3 dB exchange (3.1), the 80.0 dBA threshold (2.3), sampled time (2.4), partial surveys (2.5/3.3), the TWA formula (4.1), half-up rounding (1.2), the status bands and flags (5.1-5.3), group mean, TWA and status (6.1), and report shape and order (README) are all visible. The two manual gaps are covered by the instruction's keep-today's-step clause, and the shipped code the candidate sees defines today's step exactly.

coverage_sweep.category: Permitted input domain and needed boundaries
coverage_sweep.reason: Manual 1.4 sets the limits and instruction.md:3 excludes the open inputs. Every graded survey is checked by within_limits. The boundaries graded (80.0/79.9, 115.0/115.1, 140.0/139.9, exactly three quarters, exactly the shift, 82.0/85.0) all have defining text.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier paths agree
coverage_sweep.reason: The command, the /app/src package path and the /app/tools driver path in instruction.md match what the verifier invokes and checks. No broken template text or leftover test sentinels appear.
examples/press-shop-day.json is an ungraded illustration within the section 1 limits. The instruction states the rules hold beyond it, and the sealed families follow the manual when traced.

coverage_sweep.category: Hidden tie-breaks, rounding or representation-specific grading
coverage_sweep.reason: Group order is ASCII, as the README documents. TWA rounding is half-up to a tenth and compared exactly, both disclosed. Dose is compared within a disclosed tolerance. Worker rows may carry extra keys, and group rows are barred only from the ceiling and impulse keys that 6.1 excludes. The verifier accepts int or float for dose and twa.

coverage_sweep.category: Instruction and test agree; hidden fixtures do not define correctness
coverage_sweep.reason: The differential and sealed below-three-quarters and above-ceiling expectations follow what today's visible code computes from the manual's figures. No sealed file brings in a rule found nowhere else.

Keeping the ceiling clamp does not conflict with 'add no exception, clamp or guard', because the clamp already exists and the rule forbids only additions. The instruction also requires unchanged figures where the manual is silent. The byte-identical driver requirement can be met.

rules: keep today's step below three quarters
manual 2.4 sampled time includes readings from 40 to 79.9 dBA
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: HC4-0037 V1: shift 480, 120 min at 88 and 120 min at 70. Manual sampled time is 240, which is below 360 and below 480, so the dose is 50 x 480 / 240 = 100. The sealed value is 100.0, consistent with 'from the figures the manual does define'.

rules: keep today's step below three quarters
manual 2.2 a run at 0.0 is not a reading
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: HC4-0037 V2 and HC4-0018 B1: 0.0 runs stay out of sampled time. B1 has sampled time 0, which gives today's 0.0 dose and a null TWA.

rules: the counted level above the ceiling is today's min(level, 115)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: HC4-0019 Y1: 20 min at 118.5 is counted at 115, the survey is partial (420 of 480), projected by 480/420 to 5178.55; this matches the sealed value.

rules: 6.1 a group carries no flag and its status comes from the group TWA alone
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: HC4-0039 G1: both members are impulse-flagged and over, yet the group's TWA is 78.0, so the group is 'below'. The same holds for HC4-0035 MOXEK302.

rules: 1.2 status judged on the reported TWA
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Status family: T0 has an unrounded TWA of about 81.986, reported 82.0, so 'action'. T1 is about 85.03, reported 85.0, so 'action'. T2 is about 85.07, reported 85.1, so 'over'.

rules: 6.1 group dose is the mean of member shift doses
4.1 a dose of nought has no TWA
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Quiet members with dose 0.0 count in the mean (HC4-0028 G1: (0+0+200)/3 = 66.67). A group whose doses are all 0 gets twa null and status 'below'.
Splitting a run in two at its level leaves sampled time, measured dose and flags unchanged. Generated surveys carry no trap inputs, so no figure left to today's code is exercised under relabelling.
